claims.text: Replacing 2–5 at% of Mn with V in a MnNiSi-based alloy will improve mechanical ductility.
The ductility improvement from V substitution will occur through microstructural homogenization.
Low-level V substitution will largely retain the large magnetocaloric effect of the MnNiSi-based alloy.
Mn0.95V0.05NiSi represents replacement of approximately 5% of the Mn sublattice by V.
Vacuum arc melting followed by homogenization annealing will provide sufficient microstructural uniformity.
V substitution will produce a more homogeneous MnNiSi-based microstructure.
V substitution will refine the grain-boundary structure.
Grain refinement can enhance strength while retaining satisfactory ductility.
V will modify bonding and chemistry at MnNiSi grain boundaries in a way that improves ductility.
Enhanced grain-boundary bonding and reduced internal stress concentrations will promote ductility.
Low-level V substitution will leave the bulk magnetic ordering responsible for the magnetocaloric effect largely unaltered.
The V-doped alloy will have greater tensile ductility than identically processed undoped MnNiSi.
The V-doped alloy will have a modestly greater yield strength than identically processed undoped MnNiSi.
The V-doped alloy will retain a large magnetic entropy change and refrigerant capacity with minimal degradation relative to undoped MnNiSi.
The beneficial combination of mechanical and magnetocaloric properties is limited to V concentrations around 2–5 at%.
V concentrations significantly above 2–5 at% may alter the magnetic phase or microstructure and reduce the magnetocaloric effect.
Dopant-induced ductility improvements are well documented.
The magnetocaloric response after V substitution will depend on achieving optimal microstructural homogeneity.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis and boundary describe 2–5 at% V, but Mn0.95V0.05NiSi contains 5% V only on the Mn sublattice and approximately 1.67 at% V in the complete alloy. Thus the example composition falls below the stated 2–5 total-at% range.
